concerns.concern: The memory effect is not distinguished from well-known metastable vortex-matter phenomena near the peak effect or order–disorder transition. A quench into a disordered, strongly pinned vortex state could explain all observations, so the claimed intrinsic, order-parameter origin is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: The effect is not distinguished from conventional metastable vortex-matter phenomena, so the "intrinsic, order-parameter-rooted" attribution is not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: The data themselves show peak-effect hallmarks: non-monotonic J_c(B), a kink in V(B) at the window edge, and strong sample dependence. A single-species order–disorder transition could reproduce every observation.
concerns.quote: A single-species order–disorder transition, driven by UTe₂'s strongly field-dependent pinning and elastic moduli in this range ... could reproduce every observation.

concerns.concern: The field window where memory appears (about 7–16 T in S2) does not match the thermodynamic SC1/SC2 coexistence region (about 15–20 T). The text's placement of the S2 boundary also contradicts Extended Data Fig. 8.
concerns.quote: A window starting at 7 T lies deep in SC1 by specific-heat criteria, and no evidence is offered that SC2 components exist at 7–10 T.

concerns.concern: Heating is not excluded. A transient temperature rise followed by fast cooling is a thermal quench that would freeze a disordered vortex state, and it would naturally give stronger memory for faster turn-off. The authors' relaxation-rate argument is therefore consistent with heating rather than evidence against it.
concerns.quote: The relaxation-rate argument is therefore consistent with heating, not evidence against it.

concerns.concern: The phase diagrams are schematic and taken from other works rather than measured on the same samples. The 'memory region' is defined by the transport effect itself, which makes the argument circular. SC1.5 coexistence and two vortex species are assumed rather than shown.
concerns.quote: The purple "memory region" is defined by the transport effect itself, which makes the argument circular.

concerns.concern: The pulse-delta measurement mode means the probe and erase sweeps may themselves consist of abrupt on/off pulses. Since even ~10 µs pulses write the state, the distinction between 'pump', 'probe', 'equilibrium' and 'out-of-equilibrium' is undefined.
concerns.quote: It is then unclear why the probe and erase sweeps do not themselves act as pumps, and which settings differentiate "pump" from "probe."

concerns.concern: The argument from the low-temperature onset is not physical. Metastable disordered vortex phases are also most robust at low T, and vanishing near 0.6 K is expected for thermally activated annealing. The analogy to the intrinsic diode effect does not hold.
concerns.quote: The low-temperature argument is not physical. Its analogy to the intrinsic diode effect (ref. 49) does not hold

concerns.concern: Key literature on metastable vortex states, current-pulse switching of J_c, and the peak effect in NbSe₂, CeRu₂ and other materials is neither cited nor compared with.
concerns.quote: Key works are neither cited nor discussed

concerns.concern: The authors do not state explicitly what in the measured response is specifically two-component. 'Intrinsic' is also used ambiguously, since vortex order–disorder metastability is intrinsic to vortex matter without implying triplet or multiphase order.
concerns.quote: bulk vortex order–disorder metastability is intrinsic to vortex matter, but it is not evidence for triplet or multiphase order.

concerns.concern: Thermometry is inadequate. Temperature traces are only in an unprovided Supplementary Information, and the thermometer sits on the mixing chamber and cannot resolve fast local heating. Contact resistances, dissipated energies, heat capacity and thermal time constants are not reported.
concerns.quote: The thermometer is at the mixing chamber, not on the sample, and cannot resolve local heating on 10 µs–ms timescales.

concerns.concern: The shift of the memory window between samples of different RRR is attributed to crystalline quality without evidence. Such a shift points to pinning and disorder rather than a sharp thermodynamic boundary.
concerns.quote: The shift of the window ... is attributed to "crystalline quality" without evidence. It points to pinning and disorder rather than a sharp thermodynamic boundary.

concerns.concern: Detailed data come mainly from the lowest-quality crystal. The cleanest crystal (RRR 395) was never measured with the pump/erase protocol, so the dependence on disorder, which would distinguish pinning from an order-parameter origin, is untested.
concerns.quote: The cleanest crystal, S3 (RRR 395), was measured only by ac lock-in resistivity (Fig. 4h), with no pump/erase protocol.

concerns.concern: The ~20° angular cutoff is measured at a field where S2 is still below SC2. Rotating the field changes B_c2, reduced field and pinning regime, so the cutoff and the V(θ) jump may reflect a pinning change rather than loss of SC2. No independent probe locates SC2 versus angle on the same sample.
concerns.quote: The angular cutoff is not specific evidence for SC2.

concerns.concern: The effect is small (ΔJ ~0.2–0.5 A cm⁻² on J_c ~1–2 A cm⁻²) and is defined at a 1 µV threshold amid µV-level noise. No error bars, noise floors or reproducibility data are given, the heat maps look partly noise-textured, and robustness to the voltage criterion is not shown.
concerns.quote: No error bars, noise floor, cycle-to-cycle distributions or trace-to-trace reproducibility of the equilibrium curve are shown for the heat maps

concerns.concern: Point-like spot-welded contacts on a thick crystal give inhomogeneous current injection, current crowding and local heating. Edge and surface-barrier contamination, a known source of pulse-dependent metastable high-J_c states, is not explored.
concerns.quote: Edge and surface-barrier contamination (Paltiel et al.) is a known source of pulse-dependent metastable high-J_c states.

concerns.concern: Critical-state remanence is not quantitatively excluded. The claim that Bean-model remanence is insensitive to turn-off is incorrect, because flux creep and induced fields make remanent current distributions rate dependent. The polarity-symmetry counter-argument is left implicit and untested.
concerns.quote: The argument that a Bean-model process "should be insensitive to how the current is turned off" is not generally correct.

concerns.concern: The current waveform actually delivered to the sample is unverified. The source's point rate and bandwidth, plus long wiring in the magnet, may distort fast edges, yet the duration and turn-off-rate dependence relies on these parameters.
concerns.quote: A 10 µs "duration" defined by 100 points, or α = 500 A cm⁻² ms⁻¹, may not be realised as specified.

concerns.concern: No local or bulk probe shows that the two states differ in vortex structure. The ~0.5–0.6 K temperature scale is not linked to any independently measured energy scale of SC1/SC2 competition.
concerns.quote: No local or bulk probe shows that the two states differ in vortex structure.

concerns.concern: The theoretical model builds in the binary result through a hand-crafted double-well potential, phase-dependent damping and several tuned parameters. It fails to reproduce the graded dependences, timescales and field/temperature/angle windows, and makes no falsifiable predictions.
concerns.quote: The phase-dependent damping is introduced by hand to make φ "stick" at π, so the model reproduces the binary outcome ... by construction.

concerns.concern: The model has no microscopic link to SC1/SC2. Its simulated curves show discrete jumps unlike the smooth data, and the Josephson timescales it implies are not reconciled with the observed millisecond dynamics.
concerns.quote: The Josephson timescales implied by φ̇ = 2eV/ħ are not reconciled with the observed ms dynamics.

concerns.concern: The phase variable φ is described inconsistently: as a junction phase, as Cooper-pair momentum, as a domain-wall configuration and as a pair-density-wave. Coarse-graining a junction-free crystal to a single phase is not justified.
concerns.quote: These are different objects, and the coarse-graining from a junction-free mm-scale crystal to a single phase variable is not justified.

concerns.concern: The claim that inversion symmetry forces the second minimum to φ = π is not demonstrated for an inhomogeneous state. A uniform π winding is a finite-momentum state, so calling it 'inhomogeneous domain walls' changes the physics.
concerns.quote: The claim that inversion symmetry forces the second minimum to φ = π is not demonstrated for an inhomogeneous state.

concerns.concern: Using γ as a proxy for the injected current when constructing J–V curves is unclear and appears inconsistent with the model's Eq. (2).
concerns.quote: Treating "γ as a proxy to the injected current J" when constructing J–V curves is unclear and appears inconsistent with Eq. (2).

concerns.concern: The model conflates flux-flow damping with pinning force when explaining the higher J_c, although in RSJ models J_c is set by the potential slope, not by damping.
concerns.quote: In RSJ, J_c is set by max U′, not by damping.

concerns.concern: Two pictures, a glassy disordered vortex state and a grid of SC1/SC2 domain walls, are offered without being reconciled.
concerns.quote: A "glassy vortex state with higher disorder" and a "grid of SC1/SC2 domain walls" are both offered without reconciliation.

concerns.concern: The finite-q and diode scenarios raised in the Methods would generally predict nonreciprocity, which is not tested.
concerns.quote: The finite-q and diode scenarios raised in the Methods would generally predict nonreciprocity, which is not tested.

concerns.concern: Some physics terminology is inaccurate. 'Minimise entropy' and 'stronger pinning forces between vortices' are wrong, since pinning is vortex–defect and the enhanced J_c of a disordered lattice follows from Larkin–Ovchinnikov-type arguments.
concerns.quote: "Minimise entropy" and "stronger pinning forces between vortices" are inaccurate. Pinning is vortex–defect

concerns.concern: Non-volatility and multi-hour persistence are asserted without retention data, without the temperature dependence of decay, and without documenting field and temperature stability during the wait.
concerns.quote: "Non-volatile" and "persists for at least several hours" are stated without retention data

concerns.concern: Only about five write/erase cycles are shown. Endurance, read margin, switching thresholds and their distributions, stochasticity and error rates are not quantified.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1d shows only ~5 write/erase cycles. Endurance, read margin, switching thresholds and their distributions, stochasticity and error rates are not quantified.

concerns.concern: Readout is dissipative: one state is read in flux flow. Whether repeated probing near J_c anneals the stored state is not tested, though flux flow should anneal a quenched glass.
concerns.quote: Whether repeated probing near J_c anneals the stored state is not tested.

concerns.concern: Write and erase energies and the ON/OFF voltage ratio versus field and temperature are not reported.
concerns.quote: They should also report write and erase energies and the ON/OFF voltage ratio versus field and temperature.

concerns.concern: Claims to be the 'first' electrically controlled superconducting memory are inaccurate, given existing current-controlled vortex, kinetic-inductance and nanowire memories.
concerns.quote: "First" electrically controlled superconducting memory, and "electrically-controllable memory ... has remained elusive," are inaccurate.

concerns.concern: Calling the device 'controlled solely by electrical stimuli', 'ultralow-power' and 'non-dissipative' is overstated. It needs 7–20 T fields and sub-kelvin temperatures, writing requires flux flow, and one read state is resistive.
concerns.quote: "Ultralow-power," "non-dissipative," "read and write while superconducting." Writing requires driving into flux flow, and one read state is resistive.

concerns.concern: The nW-to-pW power-scaling estimate ignores magnet, cryogenic and write overheads. It also assumes the bulk physics survives at micron scale, where edge and surface pinning dominate.
concerns.quote: The ~1 nW → ≲1 pW estimate ignores magnet, cryogenic and write overheads.

concerns.concern: The comparison to nanometre-sized silicon elements rests on a reference about intrinsic carrier concentration in Si, which does not support it.
concerns.quote: The comparison to "nanometre-sized silicon elements" rests on a reference on intrinsic carrier concentration in Si (ref. 59), which does not support it.

concerns.concern: The AI energy-consumption framing and the Majorana/topological quantum computation outlook are speculative and not supported by the data.
concerns.quote: The AI energy-consumption framing and the Majorana/topological quantum computation outlook are not supported by the data.

concerns.concern: The Methods call the state a 'long-lived transient', while the main text says it is not transiently metastable; the wording needs harmonising.
concerns.quote: The Methods call the state "long-lived transient," whereas the main text says it is "not transiently metastable."

concerns.concern: Axis labels in Extended Data Fig. 1 are wrong, and the units of α are inconsistent between Extended Data Fig. 5 and the rest of the paper.
concerns.quote: Ext. Data Fig. 1 axis labels "J_ex (ms)" and "J/α (ms)" are wrong.

concerns.concern: The Methods contain a typo ('global minimum at π = 0').
concerns.quote: The Methods contain the typo "global minimum at π = 0."

concerns.concern: References 26 and 57 are duplicates.
concerns.quote: Refs. 26 and 57 are duplicates.
